FN-EGRP9C2-1
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 126
Committee: Public Safety and Homeland Sponsor: Representative Leigh Hulsey
Security
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver Date: 02/12/2024
House Bill 126 as introduced would increase the administrative obligations of the Alabama
Firefighters' Personnel Standards and Education Commission and the Alabama Department of
Public Health to require the implementation of annual training on interacting with individuals
with sensory needs or invisible disabilities, as part of continuing education requirements for
fire-protection personnel and certified volunteer firefighters, and emergency medical service
personnel, respectively. This bill would require both agencies to collaborate with a non-profit
company to administer this training and provide it without compensation.

FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 126
Committee: Public Safety and Homeland Sponsor: Representative Leigh Hulsey
Security
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver Date: 02/21/2024
House Bill 126 as reported by the Committee on Public Safety and Homeland Security would
increase the administrative obligations of the Alabama Firefighters' Personnel Standards and
Education Commission and the Alabama Department of Public Health to require training on
interacting with individuals with sensory needs or invisible disabilities, as part of continuing
education requirements for certain trainees, fire-protection personnel and certified volunteer
firefighters, and emergency medical service personnel, respectively. This bill would require both
agencies to collaborate with a non-profit company to administer this training and provide it
without compensation.

House Bill 126
Committee: Veterans, Military Affairs, & Public Safety Sponsor: Representative Leigh Hulsey
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver Date: 03/20/2024
House Bill 126 as passed the House of Representatives would increase the administrative
obligations of the Alabama Firefighters' Personnel Standards and Education Commission and
the Alabama Department of Public Health to require training on interacting with individuals
with sensory needs or invisible disabilities, as part of continuing education requirements for
certain recently certified fire-protection trainees, fire-protection personnel and certified
volunteer firefighters, and emergency medical service personnel, respectively. This bill would
require both agencies to collaborate with a non-profit company to administer this training and
provide it without compensation.
